```{r}
#| label: setup
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
here::i_am("manuscript/appendix.qmd")
root <- here::here()
source(file.path(root, "R", "piaac_prepare.R"))
source(file.path(root, "R", "estimators.R"))
source(file.path(root, "R", "country_summaries.R"))
source(file.path(root, "R", "figures.R"))
source(file.path(root, "R", "latex_tables.R"))
paper <- root
fig_dir <- file.path(root, "output", "figures")
latex <- knitr::is_latex_output()
options(piaac.stars = "ilr")
knitr::write_bib(c("base", "haven", "ggplot2", "patchwork", "knitr"), file = "packages.bib")

# Every number in this document is read from results written by the pipeline:
# R/03_estimate.R (results/, results_decile/) and R/04_mediation.R
# (results_mediation/, results_mediation_decile/). Nothing is typed in.
R <- function(f) readRDS(file.path(root, "results", paste0(f, ".rds")))
M <- function(f, dir = "results_mediation") readRDS(file.path(root, dir, paste0(f, ".rds")))
# Extended sample: earnings decile in 19 countries. Coefficients on the decile (1-10) are
# divided by 10, so that 100 x estimate is in percentile points of the national earnings
# distribution. Sorting results have tasks as the outcome and are not rescaled.
rescale10 <- function(x) lapply(x, function(d) { d$estimate <- d$estimate / 10; d$se <- d$se / 10; d })
RD <- function(f, rescale = TRUE) {
  x <- readRDS(file.path(root, "results_decile", paste0("art_", f, ".rds")))
  if (rescale) rescale10(x) else x
}
# Total and direct effects from mediate(), arranged as a specification sequence:
# "SKILL|M0" is the total effect and "SKILL|M4" the direct effect net of the 4 blocks.
med_seq <- function(ch) lapply(ch, function(r) do.call(rbind, lapply(c(total = "M0", direct = "M4"), function(m) {
  part <- names(which(c(total = "M0", direct = "M4") == m))
  x <- r[r$term %in% paste0("mean|", trait_names, "|", part), ]
  data.frame(term = paste0(sub("^mean\\|(\\w+)\\|.*$", "\\1", x$term), "|", m),
             estimate = x$estimate, se = x$se, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) })))
res <- list(
  ch = M("art_channels"), rho = M("art_rho"), sens = M("med_sens_grid"), ind = R("art_industry_split"),
  yard = R("art_yardstick"), rv1 = R("rv_full"),
  sc = R("art_skills_compl"), pc = R("art_pc_variants"),
  A = R("art_mp_A"), B = R("art_mp_B"), C = R("art_mp_C"), A0 = R("art_mp_nojob_A"), B0 = R("art_mp_nojob_B"),
  own = R("art_alloc_own"), job = R("art_alloc_job"), cell = R("art_alloc_cell"), tenure = R("art_alloc_tenure"),
  sup = M("art_channels_sup"), occ2 = M("art_channels_occ2"), broadA = M("art_channels_broadA"),
  m1 = R("m1"))
res$seq <- med_seq(res$ch)
res <- c(res, list(
  d_ch = rescale10(M("art_channels", "results_mediation_decile")),
  d_sc = RD("skills_compl"), d_pc = RD("pc_variants"),
  d_A = RD("mp_A"), d_B = RD("mp_B"), d_C = RD("mp_C"), d_A0 = RD("mp_nojob_A"), d_B0 = RD("mp_nojob_B"),
  d_own = RD("alloc_own", FALSE), d_cell = RD("alloc_cell", FALSE)))
res$d_seq <- med_seq(res$d_ch)
med_info <- M("run_info")
flow <- utils::read.csv(file.path(paper, "results", "sample_flow.csv"))
countries <- names(res$seq)
K <- length(countries)
A_countries <- names(res$A)
countries_d <- names(res$d_seq)
K_d <- length(countries_d)
added_d <- setdiff(countries_d, countries)
N_d <- sum(utils::read.csv(file.path(paper, "results_decile", "countries.csv"))$n)
# Bridge between the outcomes: mediation estimates in the twelve countries with both.
bridge <- local({
  a <- unlist(lapply(countries, function(cc) res$ch[[cc]]$estimate))
  b <- unlist(lapply(countries, function(cc) res$d_ch[[cc]]$estimate[match(res$ch[[cc]]$term, res$d_ch[[cc]]$term)]))
  c(r = cor(a, b), slope = sum(a * b) / sum(a^2)) })
trait_names <- names(trait_label)

# Summary rows (countries and Mean) for one term, memoised.
.memo <- new.env()
S <- function(r, term) {
  key <- paste(r, term)
  if (is.null(.memo[[key]])) .memo[[key]] <- country_and_summary(res[[r]], term)
  .memo[[key]]
}
row_of <- function(r, term, stat = "Mean") { x <- S(r, term); x[x$country == stat, ] }
# Numbers for display, with a true minus sign (U+2212).
f <- function(x, d = 1) { x <- round(x, d); x[x == 0] <- 0
  sub("^-", "−", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d)) }
# v(): estimate; vc(): estimate [95% CI] -- x100 by default.
# Negative scale reverses the sign (e.g. to describe a gap that widens).
v  <- function(r, term, stat = "Mean", d = 1, scale = 100) f(scale * row_of(r, term, stat)$estimate, d)
vc <- function(r, term, stat = "Mean", d = 1, scale = 100) {
  x <- row_of(r, term, stat)
  b <- sort(scale * c(x$lo, x$hi))
  paste0(f(scale * x$estimate, d), " [", f(b[1], d), ", ", f(b[2], d), "]")
}
# Table cells: estimate with stars over (SE); median over [95% interval].
est_star <- function(x, d = 2, scale = 100) paste0(f(scale * x$estimate, d), sig(x$p))
se_par   <- function(x, d = 2, scale = 100) paste0("(", f(scale * x$se, d), ")")
ci_br    <- function(x, d = 2, scale = 100) {
  b <- sort(scale * c(x$lo, x$hi)); paste0("[", f(b[1], d), ", ", f(b[2], d), "]") }
npos <- function(r, term) row_of(r, term)$n_pos
nneg <- function(r, term) row_of(r, term)$n_neg
i2 <- function(r, term) round(100 * row_of(r, term)$I2)
words <- c("none", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight",
           "nine", "ten", "eleven", "twelve", "thirteen", "fourteen", "fifteen", "sixteen",
           "seventeen", "eighteen", "nineteen")
w <- function(n) format(n)   # JOB version: numbers as digits
country_name <- function(cc) unname(country_label[cc])
listc <- function(x) if (length(x) < 2) x else if (length(x) == 2) paste(x, collapse = " and ") else
  paste0(paste(x[-length(x)], collapse = ", "), ", and ", x[length(x)])   # serial comma
which_c <- function(r, term, side = c("pos", "neg")) {
  side <- match.arg(side); x <- S(r, term); x <- x[!x$country %in% c("Mean", "Median"), ]
  country_name(x$country[if (side == "pos") x$lo > 0 else x$hi < 0])
}
share <- function(num, den, r = "ch") round(100 * row_of(r, num)$estimate / row_of(r, den)$estimate)
pp <- "percentile points"
# vcp(): estimate with the % sign before the interval, e.g. "3.9% [3.2, 4.6]".
vcp <- function(...) sub("^(\\S+) ", "\\1% ", vc(...))
stars_note <- "\\* p < 0.10, \\*\\* p < 0.05, \\*\\*\\* p < 0.01."

d_ <- load_country_data(countries)
N_total <- sum(sapply(d_, nrow))
fmtN <- function(n) format(n, big.mark = ",")

fig <- function(p, name, width = 6.5, height = 4) {
  save_figure(p, name, fig_dir, width, height)
  knitr::include_graphics(file.path(fig_dir, paste0(name, if (latex) ".pdf" else ".png")), dpi = if (latex) NA else if (knitr::pandoc_to("docx")) 300 else 110)
}
```

# Appendix {.unnumbered}

*Returns to non-cognitive skills: Do they arise through education, job sorting, or work tasks?*

This appendix accompanies the study. Section A reports the sample construction (Table A1); Section B the total, indirect and direct effects for every country, for log hourly wages in the 12 main countries and for the earnings decile in the 19 countries of the decile sample (Tables A2–A5); Section C the skill × job-demand interactions under 3 demand measures and the sensitivity of the mediation estimates to the occupation and sector block (Tables A6 and A7); Section D the robustness checks summarized in the study (Figures A1 and A2) and the indirect effect through industry split by industry (Figure A3). Significance marks (\* p < 0.10, \*\* p < 0.05, \*\*\* p < 0.01) and all definitions follow the study.

# A. Sample construction

```{r}

               experience = "Experience and tenure", job_sorting = "Occupation and sector",
               industry = "Industry", tasks = "Tasks", direct = "Direct effect")
```

```{r}
            wage = "Positive hourly earnings and survey weight",
            skills = "Valid gender, education, personality scores, and plausible values",
            tasks = "Complete responses to the 9 task items",

       space_before = length(stages), notes = notes_flow)
```

# B. Country-level estimates

```{r}
#| label: tbl-s07
#| tbl-cap: "Country-specific mediation estimates: total effect and direct effect of each non-cognitive skill (%, 95% intervals)"
spec_cols <- c(M0 = "A. Total effect", M4 = "B. Direct effect (net of all 6 blocks)")
ord_rows <- c(countries[order(country_name(countries))], "Mean")
ret_rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(spec_cols), function(m) {
  x <- country_and_summary(res$seq, paste0(trait_names, "|", m))
  t(sapply(ord_rows, function(cc) c(if (cc %in% countries) country_name(cc) else cc,
    sapply(trait_names, function(tr) { y <- x[x$country == cc & x$term == paste0(tr, "|", m), ]
      paste0(f(100 * y$estimate), " ", ci_br(y, 1)) })))) }))
notes_ar <- paste("*Notes:* Total effect (regression with the baseline controls and the 5 non-cognitive skills) and",
  "direct effect (net of education, cognitive skills, experience and tenure, occupation and sector, industry, and tasks) per SD of each",
  "skill, from mediate (Tingley et al. 2014) with the mean of the 10 plausible values of literacy; 95%",
  "quasi-Bayesian intervals.")
ltable(ret_rows, header = c("", trait_label), align = "lccccc", long = TRUE,
       panels = setNames(c(1, 14), spec_cols),
       space_before = 13, tabcolsep = 4, notes = notes_ar)
```

# C. Job-demand interactions and the occupation block

```{r}
#| label: tbl-s05
#| tbl-cap: "Wage-regression interactions between matched skills and job demands under 3 demand measures (%)"
pairs <- paste(trait_names, c("influence", "organisation", "learning", "pressure", "cooperation"), sep = ":")
pr_rows <- c(pairs, "matched_mean", "mismatched_mean", "match_premium")
pr_lab <- c(paste(trait_label, "×", tolower(matched_task_label[trait_names])),
            "Mean of matched interactions", "Mean of mismatched interactions", "Match premium")
pr_grid <- function(fun) cbind(pr_lab, sapply(c("A", "C", "B", "A0", "B0"), function(r)
  sapply(pr_rows, function(t) fun(row_of(r, t)))))
notes_pairs <- paste("*Notes:* Interaction between each non-cognitive skill and the demand for its matched task,",
  "mean of countries with standard errors in parentheses. A: co-worker demand in two-digit",
  "occupation cells with two-digit occupation fixed effects (7 countries). C: co-worker demand",
  "in broad job cells. B: the respondent's own report. Job controls: experience and tenure, occupation group, sector,",
  "establishment size, and industry (two-digit occupations for A). The match premium is the mean of the 5",
  "matched interactions minus the mean of the 20 mismatched ones. Co-worker cells need at least 15",
  "respondents; broad job cells fall back from occupation × sector × establishment size to occupation × sector and then to occupation.",
  stars_note)
ltable(pr_grid(est_star), sub = pr_grid(se_par),
       header = c("", "Co-worker,\ntwo-digit (A)", "Co-worker,\nbroad cell (C)", "Own\nreport (B)",
                  "Co-worker,\ntwo-digit (A)", "Own\nreport (B)"),
       align = "lccccc", space_before = 6,
       groups = list(list(list(label = "With job controls", from = 2, to = 4),
                          list(label = "Without job controls", from = 5, to = 6))),
       notes = notes_pairs)
```

# D. Robustness

```{r}
#| label: sens-data
oriv <- lapply(R("rob_oriv"), function(r) transform(r, term = paste0("mean|", term)))
B_c <- names(oriv)
checks <- list(
  "Main estimate" = res$m1,
  "Numeracy instead of literacy" = R("rob_numeracy"),
  "Literacy and numeracy" = R("rob_both"),
  "Untrimmed earnings" = R("rob_untrimmed"),
  "Earnings without bonuses" = R("rob_nobonus"),
  "Without Poland" = res$m1[setdiff(countries, "POL")],
  "Six-item countries, uncorrected" = res$m1[B_c],
  "Six-item countries, split-half IV" = oriv)
rob_m <- function(lab, tr) { x <- country_and_summary(checks[[lab]], paste0("mean|", tr)); x[x$country == "Mean", ] }
rv_ <- function(lab, tr) f(100 * rob_m(lab, tr)$estimate)
loo <- sapply(countries, function(cc) { p <- country_and_summary(res$m1[setdiff(countries, cc)], paste0("mean|", trait_names))
  p <- p[p$country == "Mean", ]; 100 * p$estimate[match(paste0("mean|", trait_names), p$term)] })
main_m1 <- sapply(trait_names, function(tr) 100 * rob_m("Main estimate", tr)$estimate)
loo_dev <- max(abs(loo - main_m1))
re <- pool_terms(res$m1); re <- re[match(paste0("mean|", trait_names), re$term), ]
re_dev <- max(abs(100 * re$pooled - main_m1))
bench_w <- row_of("rv1", "bench_wage")$estimate
bench_t <- max(sapply(trait_names, function(tr) row_of("rv1", paste0("bench_trait|", tr))$estimate))
rv_min <- min(sapply(trait_names, function(tr) row_of("rv1", paste0("rv|", tr))$estimate))
rv_max <- max(sapply(trait_names, function(tr) row_of("rv1", paste0("rv|", tr))$estimate))
sup_ <- function(tr, pt) f(100 * row_of("sup", paste0("mean|", tr, "|", pt))$estimate, 2)
occ_ <- function(r, tr, pt) { x <- country_and_summary(res[[r]], paste0("mean|", tr, "|", pt)); f(100 * x$estimate[x$country == "Mean"], 2) }
occ_num <- function(r, tr, pt) { x <- country_and_summary(res[[r]], paste0("mean|", tr, "|", pt)); 100 * x$estimate[x$country == "Mean"] }
occ_rem_dev <- max(sapply(trait_names, function(tr) abs(occ_num("occ2", tr, "direct") - occ_num("broadA", tr, "direct"))))
```

The returns net of education and cognitive skills change little under alternative specifications: numeracy instead of literacy, literacy and numeracy together, untrimmed earnings, earnings without bonuses, and the sample without Poland (@fig-s2). No single country moves a mean return by more than `r f(loo_dev, 1)`%, and a random-effects pooling of the 12 countries differs from the simple mean by at most `r f(re_dev, 1)`%. Measurement error in the 3-item scores works in the other direction: in the 7 countries with 6-item scales, a split-half instrumental-variable correction [@gillen2019] raises the extraversion return from `r rv_("Six-item countries, uncorrected", "EXTR")` to `r rv_("Six-item countries, split-half IV", "EXTR")`%.

@fig-s3 reports the robustness values of @cinelli2020. To reduce a direct effect to zero, an unobserved confounder would have to explain between `r f(100 * rv_min, 1)`% and `r f(100 * rv_max, 1)`% of the residual variance of log wages, and the same share of the residual variance of the non-cognitive skill. For comparison, parental education explains `r f(100 * bench_w, 1)`% of the residual variance of wages and at most `r f(100 * bench_t, 1)`% of the residual variance of a non-cognitive skill.

```{r}
#| label: fig-s2
#| fig-cap: "Adjusted wage-regression estimates (net of education and cognitive skills) under alternative specifications and samples. Mean of countries with 95% intervals (%); the dashed line marks the main estimate. The last 2 rows use the 7 countries with 6-item scales; the split-half instrumental-variable estimate corrects for measurement error in the 3-item scores. The second 3-item half is reconstructed from the published 3-item and 6-item scores under the assumption of parallel items, so this check is approximate."
fig(fig_robustness_checks(checks, unit = "%"), "fig8_robustness", 6.5, 3.3)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-s3
#| fig-cap: "Sensitivity of the direct effects to unobserved confounding (Cinelli–Hazlett robustness values, outcome equation with all 6 blocks): the share of the residual variance of both log wages and the non-cognitive skill that an unobserved confounder would need to explain to reduce the direct effect to zero. Circles are countries; the diamond is the mean of countries with its 95% interval. The shaded area extends to the larger of the two parental-education benchmarks (mean of countries)."
fig(fig_robustness_values(res$rv1), "fig9_robustness_values", 6.2, 3)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-s4
#| fig-cap: "Indirect effect through industry, split by industry. For each ISIC Rev. 4 section, the contribution is the effect of the skill on the probability of working in that industry times the industry's wage differential, which is shown in parentheses relative to the average job of workers with comparable education, cognitive skills, experience and tenure, occupation, sector and tasks. Mean of 12 countries with 95% intervals from the replicate weights and plausible values (%). Industries are ordered by their wage differential. Diamond: the indirect effect through industry from mediate, estimated separately; the industry terms add up to it up to the averaging of plausible values and the omitted not-reported category."
fig(fig_industry_split(res$ind, res$ch), "fig10_industry_split", 6.8, 5.6)
```
